memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "So that day Esau started on his way back to Seir. Jacob, however, went to Sukkoth, where he built a place for himself and made shelters for his livestock. That is why the place is called Sukkoth." - Gen 33:16-17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The brothers part in peace — Esau heading home to Seir, Jacob moving on. But notice where Jacob goes. He stops at a place he names Sukkoth, where he "built a place for himself and made shelters for his livestock." He puts down roots, if only for a time. It is the first sign of settling.

Now, this was not wrong in itself. But we do well to remember Jacob's larger story. Years earlier at Bethel, Jacob had vowed that if God brought him safely home, "the LORD will be my God" (Gen 28:21), and God had specifically told him to return to Bethel (Gen 31:13). Yet here Jacob is settling at Sukkoth, and soon at Shechem — not yet arriving where he had promised to go. He is close to full obedience, but not quite there.

This is a gentle warning for us. It is possible to obey God most of the way and then stop short of the finish. We start well, we come far, and then we settle down comfortably just short of what God asked. "Almost there" can quietly become "far enough."

Is there a place God has called you to that you have stopped just short of reaching — a step of obedience, a work, a surrender you have delayed? Do not build your shelters halfway. Ask God for the resolve to go all the way to the "Bethel" He has called you to.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where might I be stopping short of full obedience to God?
2. Have I settled comfortably "almost" where God called me?
3. What "Bethel" is God calling me to reach completely?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, keep me from stopping short of full obedience. Where I have settled halfway, give me resolve to go all the way to the place You have called me. Amen.
